physical_harm: Double murder of daughter aged 12 years and her father aged 50 years; severe injuries
motive: Loan not returned to deceased No.2 victim
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of the prosecution, including the FSL report, credibility of witnesses, footprints of the offender, narration of incident by the circumstantial witness, identification of the accused/weapon, and presence of light in the murder scene.
witness_credibility: The Supreme Court assessed the main witnesses as credible, specifically noting that there was no reason to disbelieve the evidence of PWs 1 and 2, who were injured eye witnesses, and that the High Court failed to consider the evidence of PWs 20-22.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 18.09.2005; Trial judgment: 31.07.2008; High Court decision: 17.08.2012; Supreme Court decision: 09.02.2017
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Suyodhan Byrapaneni, V. Sridhar Reddy, V. N. Raghupathy, Guntur Prabhakar, Ms. Prerna Singh, D. Mahesh Babu; Counsel for the State: Ms. Tatini Basu
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence; High Court: Acquittal; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, order set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused had the requisite motive for committing the offence, the weapon (sickle) used can be convincingly linked to the injuries caused on the deceased, and the evidence including FSL report, credibility of witnesses, footprints of the offender, narration of incident by the circumstantial witness, identification of the accused/weapon, and presence of light in the murder scene all lead to the guilt of the accused.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court was right in coming to its conclusion by observing that the prosecution has failed to establish the motive for the commission of the offence by the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the High Court's order was perverse and not sustainable in the eyes of law, and that the well-reasoned order of the trial court should be affirmed.
precedent_relied_upon: Medical Jurisprudence on Toxicology by Dr. K. S. Reddy
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court's order was found to be perverse and not sustainable in the eyes of law, and the trial court's well-reasoned conviction and sentence should be affirmed.
other_sentence_order: The Supreme Court directed the concerned Police Authorities to take custody of the respondent forthwith to serve out the remainder of sentence imposed by the Trial Court.
